skills.name: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment

note.text:
The perpendicular bisector of a segment [AB] is the line that passes through the midpoint of [AB] and is perpendicular to (AB). We often call it (Δ) and write (Δ) ⊥ (AB). It cuts [AB] into two equal parts at a right angle (90°).
To construct it with ruler and compasses:
1. Open the compasses to more than half of AB.
2. With the point on A, draw an arc above [AB] and an arc below it.
3. With the same opening and the point on B, draw arcs that cross the first two.
4. Join the two crossing points with a ruler: this line is the perpendicular bisector.
If the compasses are opened to half of AB or less, the arcs do not cross.

worked_example.problem: AB = {ab} cm. Explain how to construct the perpendicular bisector (Δ) of [AB], and say where it cuts [AB].
steps: Half of AB is {ab} ÷ {two} = {ab / two} cm, so open the compasses to more than {ab / two} cm, for example {r} cm.
With the point on A, draw arcs above and below [AB]; with the same opening and the point on B, draw arcs that cross them.
Join the two crossing points: this is (Δ). It cuts [AB] at its midpoint M, with AM = MB = {ab / two} cm, at {ninety}°.
worked_example.answer: (Δ) passes through M, the midpoint of [AB], and (Δ) ⊥ (AB).

cards.idea: The perpendicular bisector of [AB] does two things: it passes through the midpoint of [AB], and it is perpendicular to (AB).
example: (Δ) cuts [AB] at M with AM = MB.
The angle between (Δ) and (AB) is a right angle: (Δ) ⊥ (AB).

cards.idea: Open the compasses to more than half of AB, or the arcs from A and from B will not cross.
example: AB = {ab} cm: half of AB is {ab / two} cm.
Open the compasses to {r} cm, which is more than {ab / two} cm.

check.prompt: AB = {ab} cm. To construct the perpendicular bisector of [AB], which compass opening works?

misconceptions.explain: With exactly half of AB, {h} cm, the arcs only touch on [AB]: they do not cross above and below.
{s} cm is less than half of AB ({h} cm): the arcs from A and from B do not meet.

solution: The opening must be more than half of AB: more than {ab} ÷ {two} = {h} cm.

cards.idea: The perpendicular bisector cuts the segment into two equal parts, at a right angle.
example: AB = {ab} cm: (Δ) cuts [AB] at M with AM = MB = {ab / two} cm.

questions.prompt: Which line is the perpendicular bisector of [AB]?

right.text: the line through the midpoint of [AB] that is perpendicular to (AB)
the line that cuts [AB] at its midpoint, at a right angle
the line (Δ) through M, the midpoint of [AB], with (Δ) ⊥ (AB)

wrong.text: any line through the midpoint of [AB]
wrong.explain: It must also be perpendicular to (AB).
It must also pass through the midpoint of [AB].
(AB) contains the segment; the perpendicular bisector crosses it at a right angle.

wrong.text: the line through A that is perpendicular to (AB)
wrong.explain: It must pass through the midpoint of [AB], not through A.

questions.prompt: (Δ) is the perpendicular bisector of [AB] and cuts it at M. AB = {ab} cm. Find AM.

misconceptions.explain: M is the midpoint, so AM is half of AB.

solution: (Δ) passes through the midpoint of [AB], so M is the midpoint.

questions.prompt: (Δ) is the perpendicular bisector of [{L[0]}{L[1]}]. What is the size of the angle between (Δ) and ({L[0]}{L[1]}), in degrees?

misconceptions.explain: {180}° is a straight angle. Perpendicular lines make a right angle.
Perpendicular means a right angle, not half of one.

solution: The perpendicular bisector is perpendicular to the line ({L[0]}{L[1]}).
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle: {answer}°.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for constructing the perpendicular bisector of [AB] in order.

items.text: Open the compasses to more than half of AB
With the point on A, draw an arc above [AB] and an arc below it
With the same opening and the point on B, draw arcs that cross the first two
Join the two crossing points with a ruler

questions.prompt: (Δ) is the perpendicular bisector of [AB] and cuts it at M. MB = {mb} cm. Find AB.

misconceptions.explain: MB is half of AB, so AB is double MB.

solution: M is the midpoint of [AB], so AM = MB = {mb} cm.

questions.prompt: Ngwa wrote these sentences about constructing the perpendicular bisector of [AB], with AB = {ab} cm. Which sentence is wrong?

right.text: I open the compasses to {h + 2} cm
The line I draw passes through the midpoint of [AB]
The line I draw is perpendicular to (AB)
I keep the same opening for the arcs from A and from B

wrong.text: I open the compasses to {h - 1} cm
wrong.explain: {h - 1} cm is less than half of AB ({h} cm): the arcs would not cross.

wrong.text: I change the opening before drawing the arcs from B
wrong.explain: The opening must stay the same for the arcs from A and from B.

wrong.text: The line I draw passes through A
wrong.explain: The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint of [AB], not through A.
